trans-unit.source: Problem reports created by backend users, with the attached TYPO3 context and the delivery history. Reports cannot be edited: this is an audit trail, not a ticket system.
No delivery destination is enabled. Reports are stored here and can be downloaded.
Backend users can report a problem from the toolbar, from the record and file lists, from the Page module, from context menus, or while editing a record.
No report has this delivery state. Choose another filter to see more reports.
All reports have been resolved. Choose "Resolved" or "All" to see them.
The history always records who created a report. What is shared with delivery destinations depends on the privacy settings.
Deleting removes the report, its screenshot and its delivery history from TYPO3. Copies that were already sent are not affected.
Everything that is attached to the report: object metadata, backend view, system and browser.
The report has not been delivered anywhere. It is stored in this history only.
Only administrators can use Context Reports.
Delivery via %s is not enabled or not configured.
There is no failed delivery via %s to retry.
What reports contain, how long they are kept and where they are sent. Only administrators can see and change these settings.
Not saved in this module yet.
The settings were not saved. Please correct the marked fields.
Secret values that you entered were not kept; please enter them again.
Set in the TYPO3 system configuration and cannot be changed here.
Some settings are set in the TYPO3 system configuration
Values in $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['EXTENSIONS']['context_reporter'] (for example in config/system/additional.php) take precedence over this page: %s
Settings of a development version take precedence

The TYPO3 system configuration contains Context Reporter settings of a development version (EXTENSIONS › context_reporter, written to config/system/settings.php by the former Extension Configuration form). They take precedence over this page, so most fields are locked. Remove the context_reporter entry from config/system/settings.php (or config/system/additional.php), then configure Context Reporter here.
Whether reports can be created and how the project is named in reports.
When switched off, backend users cannot create reports. Stored reports remain available here.
Shown in reports, email subjects and webhook payloads. When empty, the TYPO3 site name is used (%s).
Optional key for receiving systems. Letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores.
Helps recipients tell reports of different systems apart. Automatic uses the TYPO3 application context (%s).
Which personal and technical data a report contains. The data is stored here and included in downloads, emails and webhook deliveries.
Facts about the backend user who creates a report.
The uid of the backend user. The report history uses it to show who reported a problem.
The login name of the backend user.
The name stored in the backend user record.
Required if email recipients should be able to reply to the reporter.
IDs and titles of the backend groups of the user.
Details that help to reproduce a problem.
Browser and operating system, user agent, window and screen size, pixel ratio, languages, time zone, color scheme and reduced motion.

Optional and off by default. Adds up to 10 errors and warnings of the reporting user from the TYPO3 system log of the last 30 minutes, shortened. The messages are written by TYPO3 and extensions and can contain record titles or other sensitive diagnostic text. Enable this only if everyone who receives reports may see such text.
In addition to the options on the left

The title and description entered by the reporter and the optional screenshot; the reported page, record, file or folder (type, ID, title, page, site, language, workspace); the backend module and route; links to the report and the object; the project name, identifier and environment; TYPO3 and PHP version, application context, database platform and server operating system.

Field values of records other than the title, form contents, file contents and file metadata values, cookies, sessions, request headers, passwords and API keys. Exception: the optional recent backend errors contain log messages as TYPO3 and extensions wrote them, which can include confidential diagnostic text.
The report dialog shows all data before it is sent.
Limits for new reports and how long reports are kept.
Between 100 and 15360 KB. The browser compresses larger screenshots or rejects them.
Protects against accidental floods of reports. 0 turns the limit off.
Applies to reports with their screenshots and delivery history. Reports are only removed when an administrator runs the cleanup.
Screenshots: %1$d, delivery attempts: %2$d (their report no longer exists)

Reports are stored in the table tx_contextreporter_report, screenshots in tx_contextreporter_attachment and the delivery history in tx_contextreporter_delivery. No files are written. Deleting a report also deletes its screenshot and delivery history.
Reports are kept forever, so the cleanup removes no reports. To remove old reports, choose a retention and save the settings.
Reports are kept for %1$d days. The cleanup removes reports created before %2$s.
The cleanup also removes entries whose report no longer exists (screenshots: %1$d, delivery attempts: %2$d).
The same cleanup is available on the command line, e.g. for cron jobs:
All reports created before %2$s (%1$d in total) will be deleted together with their screenshots and delivery history. This cannot be undone.
Screenshots and delivery attempts without a report will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
Cleanup finished. Removed reports: %1$d, removed orphaned entries: %2$d.
The retention has changed in the meantime. Check the preview and try again.
New reports are sent through the mail configuration of TYPO3.
Every new report is sent to the recipients as a plain text email.
Up to 20 email addresses, separated by commas or line breaks.
When empty, the TYPO3 default sender is used (%s).
Used together with the sender address.
Markers such as {project.name}, {report.title} and {report.id} are replaced.
A .txt file with markers below Resources/Private/ of an extension, e.g. EXT:my_sitepackage/Resources/Private/Templates/Email/ContextReport.txt.
Attached as PNG or JPEG file when the report has one.
The machine-readable report (context-reporter.report.v1), without the screenshot.
Sets the reporter as Reply-To. Requires "Email address" in the privacy settings.
New reports are posted as JSON to an endpoint, e.g. n8n, Make, Zapier or your own service.
Every new report is posted with the event "report.created".
An https URL, or %env(NAME)% to read it from an environment variable. A stored URL is not shown again, because webhook URLs often contain access tokens.
Signs every delivery with HMAC-SHA256 in the header X-Context-Reporter-Signature, so the receiver can verify it. A value or %env(NAME)%.
The name of the header that carries the value below, e.g. Authorization or X-Api-Key.
For example "Bearer …". A value or %env(NAME)%. The header is only sent when a value is set.
Embeds the screenshot base64-encoded in the JSON payload.
For local tests only: reports and secrets are then sent unencrypted.
Environment variable %s is not set or not valid
Leave empty to keep the current value
The mail transport is configured in the TYPO3 system configuration ($GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['MAIL']). Credentials are never shown.
Email delivery is switched off: reports are not sent by email.
The TYPO3 mail transport is "null": all emails are discarded.
The TYPO3 mail transport is "mbox": emails are written to a file on the server instead of being sent.
Emails are queued (spool "%s") and only sent when the console command "mailer:spool:send" runs.
The mail transport points to a local mail catcher such as Mailpit: emails do not reach real mailboxes.
This is a DDEV project: emails are captured by Mailpit and do not reach real mailboxes.
No sender address is set here or in the TYPO3 mail settings, so TYPO3 uses "%s". Mail servers may reject it.
The configured sender address is not valid, so TYPO3 uses "%s".
Timeout %1$d s, screenshot %2$s, redirects are not followed
Endpoint paths and secret values are never shown.
Webhook delivery is switched off: reports are not sent to the endpoint.
The endpoint refers to the environment variable %s, which is not set or does not contain a valid URL.
The configured endpoint is not a valid URL. An https URL is required unless unencrypted endpoints are allowed.
The authentication header value refers to the environment variable %s, which is not set or contains line breaks. The header is not sent.
The authentication header name or value is not valid. The header is not sent.
The signing secret refers to the environment variable %s, which is not set. Deliveries are sent unsigned.
Deliveries are not signed. Set a signing secret so the receiver can verify them.
Sends a short message without report data to the saved recipients, also while email delivery is switched off.
Save at least one recipient to send a test email.
Test email handed over to the mail transport
Recipients: %s. If the email does not arrive, check the notes of the status panel, the mail server log and the spam folder.
The test email could not be sent
Posts the event "test" without report data to the saved endpoint, also while webhook delivery is switched off. Tests are not added to the delivery history.
Save a usable endpoint to send a test webhook.
The endpoint accepted the test webhook
Use at most 100 characters without line breaks.
Use up to 64 letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter or digit.
Choose an environment or enter a name with at most 50 characters.
Choose a retention or enter a number of days between 1 and 3650.
Enter valid email addresses, separated by commas or line breaks.
Enter at least one recipient to send reports by email.
Enter a valid email address or leave the field empty.
Use at most 100 characters without line breaks.
Use at most 255 characters without line breaks.
Use an existing .txt file below Resources/Private/ of an extension, e.g. EXT:my_sitepackage/Resources/Private/Templates/Email/ContextReport.txt.
Enter an https URL (http only if unencrypted endpoints are allowed) or %env(NAME)%.
Enter an endpoint to send reports to a webhook.
The secret must not contain line breaks and may have at most 1000 characters.
Enter a valid header name, e.g. Authorization or X-Api-Key.
The value must not contain line breaks and may have at most 1000 characters.
